newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sun to sell airline stake after 1996 loss. [CORRECTED 17:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sun to sell airline stake after 1996 loss. [CORRECTED 17:55 GMT]

text.p: Belgian tour and holiday parks operator Sun International NV plans to sell its 65 percent stake in Belgian charter airline Air Belgium after running up big losses in 1996, Belga news agency reported on Thursday.
Belga said Sun was also looking for a buyer for its 46.5 percent stake in Sun Parks, a leisure resort operator.
Belga said Sun ended 1996 with group net loss of 795 million francs after a 10 million franc profit in 1995. It said poor results at Sun Parks and Air Belgium were to blame.

Belga said Sun would announce Air Belgium's buyer in June. The sale would probably result in a book loss (corrects from "book gain"), of which it had already pre-booked 300 million francs in its 1996 accounts.
Air Belgium operates two Boeing 737 aircraft.

The Brussels Stock Exchange suspended trade in Sun for the day on Thursday. The share last traded on Wednesday at 2,640 francs, off its 1997 high of 2,800 francs set on March 11, but up from 2,260 francs on January 22.
A spokesman for the bourse said trade would resume on Friday.
